questions.q: What is the main downside of putting AWS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_KEY directly into a CREATE STAGE statement?
options: Anyone reading that DDL can see the credentials, and rotating keys means editing every stage that used them
It makes the load run slower
It is not supported by Snowflake at all
It only works for internal stages
questions.explain: Hardcoded keys in DDL are visible to anyone with access to view the statement, and key rotation becomes a manual, error-prone, per-stage task.

questions.q: What does a STORAGE INTEGRATION let Snowflake do?
options: Assume a cloud identity (like an AWS IAM role) to access storage, without storing raw secret keys
Automatically create tables matching the bucket's folder structure
Convert JSON files into CSV before loading
Skip the need for a stage entirely
questions.explain: A storage integration authorizes Snowflake to assume an IAM role, service principal, or service account, replacing hardcoded credentials with a trust relationship.

questions.q: What does STORAGE_ALLOWED_LOCATIONS control on a storage integration?
options: Which bucket paths the integration is permitted to access
The warehouse size used for loads through that integration
The file format applied to loaded files
How many concurrent COPY INTO statements can run
questions.explain: STORAGE_ALLOWED_LOCATIONS restricts the integration to specific bucket paths, limiting what it can be used to access.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the four-step pattern for loading from any cloud provider's storage?
options: Authorize (storage integration), point a stage at the bucket, define the file format, then COPY INTO
Create a database, create a schema, create a table, create a view
Upload the file with PUT, then run SELECT * on the stage
Create a pipe, create a notification, create a role, then grant access
questions.explain: This four-step sequence — authorize, stage, file format, COPY INTO — is the same regardless of whether the bucket is in S3, Azure Blob, or GCS.

questions.q: What changes between loading from S3, Azure Blob, and GCS, according to this lesson?
options: Only the identity/authorization plumbing (e.g. AZURE_TENANT_ID vs. an AWS role ARN) — the overall mental model and sequence stay the same
The COPY INTO command itself is entirely different for each provider
File formats can only be used with one specific cloud provider
Stages are not supported on Azure or GCS
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that the four-step pattern is identical across providers; only the provider-specific integration fields differ.
